comments.content: The `internal` branch relies on two unchecked assumptions: (a) `getNetworks()` is non-empty and the first network has a non-null IP, and (b) `url` literally contains `host:firstMappedPort`. If a container has no network entry the iterator throws `NoSuchElementException`; if the IP is `null`/empty (Docker Desktop, some podman/rootless setups, user-defined networks) the resulting `db-url` becomes e.g. `jdbc:postgresql://null:5432/keycloak`; and if the host:port rendering differs, `String.replace` is a silent no-op and Keycloak gets the host-mapped URL that is unreachable from another container. Since this value is fed directly to `--db-url` (see `serverConfig()`), all of these turn into opaque connection failures in the clustered tests. Please validate the network/IP and fail fast (or fall back) when the URL was not rewritten.

comments.content: `BuildToolHelper.getProjectDir(Paths.get(""))` resolves the project from the **current working directory** and does not return a path in all situations (it can be `null`/throw when the working directory is not inside a Maven module, e.g. IDE or custom surefire working directories). A null result NPEs here, and chaining `.getParent().getParent()` hard-codes that the caller module is exactly two levels below the quarkus module — any other caller silently resolves `dist/target/...` and `container/Dockerfile` against the wrong base and then falls back to the remote `quay.io/keycloak/keycloak` image instead of the distribution under test. Note this is now evaluated eagerly in the constructor (it used to happen inside `getKeycloakContainer()`), so merely instantiating the distribution can now fail. Suggest resolving from the classpath directory like `Maven.resolveArtifact` does and validating the intermediate parents.
